laws.rule: Galicia's tourist stay tax (imposto galego sobre as estadías turísticas, Lei 5/2024, in force from 1 January 2025) sets rates of EUR 1 to EUR 2.50 per person per night (about A$1.59 to A$3.97), counted for up to 5 nights per stay, but gives a 100% rebate, so the regional tax itself costs nothing. A council can add its own surcharge of up to 100% of the listed rate by local ordinance, and where it does, visitors pay that surcharge through their accommodation. Cruise calls are covered too. Exempt: minors, people with a disability of 65% or more, stays in the Xunta's public pilgrim hostels (Plan Xacobeo) and youth hostels; stays for care in the Galician public health system are not taxed. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293.
laws.heading: Lei 5/2024, de 27 de decembro, arts 9 to 24 (compiled by Spain's Ministry of Finance)

laws.rule: During the high fire-danger season (época de peligro alto de incendios forestales), Galicia bans lighting campfires for recreation or cooking, and using burners or stoves that burn fuel for lighting or cooking, in farm and forest areas and the land around them (article 36.1). In forest land during the same season, smoking or making fire of any kind inside it or on the roads that border or cross it is not allowed (article 37.3). When the daily fire-risk index is very high or extreme, burning cut scrub and other waste is also banned (article 36.2). Fireworks and fire balloons for local festivals need prior council authorisation and cannot be authorised on extreme-risk days (article 37.1). The law does not set the season dates; the regional forest department publishes them. The fine scale was not read.

laws.rule: Galician Atlantic Islands National Park: camping is limited to designated places.
Galician Atlantic Islands National Park: domestic animals are prohibited except guide dogs; check access conditions for individual islands.
Galician Atlantic Islands National Park: scuba diving with weights, navigation or anchoring in park waters needs the corresponding prior authorisation.
Galician Atlantic Islands National Park: sport fishing and spearfishing are prohibited.
Galician Atlantic Islands National Park: flying drones without express park authorisation is prohibited.
Galician Atlantic Islands National Park: commercial photography without prior authorisation is prohibited.
Galician Atlantic Islands National Park: commercial filming without prior authorisation is prohibited.

Galicia's Ley 11/2010 bans anyone under 18 from drinking alcoholic drinks, and bans selling or supplying them to anyone under 18 (article 12.1 and 12.2). Sale, supply or drinking of alcoholic drinks is also banned in schools for minors, in sports grounds while the athletes or participants are mostly under 18, and in centres for minors (article 12.3). A first-time under-18 drinking offence is a light offence, fined up to EUR 601.01 in the lowest band or up to EUR 3,005.06 in the highest light band (about A$955 to A$4,775, RBA rate of 30 October 2026) (articles 22 and 27). This law is about preventing under-18 drinking; it does not itself set a region-wide ban on adults drinking in the street. Confirm any local street-drinking ordinance in the municipality you visit.

layers.authority: Xunta de Galicia (Parque Nacional Illas Atlánticas de Galicia)
layers.process: To visit the Cíes Islands in the park's high season (15 May to 15 September, per the Xunta's 2022 notice) you need a free, personal, non-transferable Xunta authorisation with a QR code. It is confirmed when you buy a boat ticket from an authorised shipping company, then emailed and downloadable from the Xunta platform (autorizacionillasatlanticas.xunta.gal). The park's management plan caps Cíes at 1,800 people a day in high season, with some places reserved for campsite guests. Press reports in 2026 repeat 1,800 but one local paper gives 2,000, and the Easter week is also named as high season: confirm the current cap and dates on the Xunta platform.

layers.authority: Xunta de Galicia, Galician Atlantic Islands National Park
layers.process: For a shipping-company day trip to Cíes or Ons during Easter and 15 May to 15 September, the park says visitors must personally request Xunta visit authorisation before buying a boat ticket. Outside those dates contact the shipping company. For overnight stays at the Cíes or Ons campsites, or other authorised Ons accommodation, contact the accommodation instead; the campsite processes the authorisation for its reserved dates.
